earned_compensation_reconciliation.basis: Core and employee deferrals (and resulting match) now use workforce prorated_annual_compensation: actual earned pay, time-weighted for compensation changes and employment, instead of pre-raise starting pay.
earned_compensation_reconciliation.verification: At pre-#978 revision 04bff1eb, the isolated characterization test passes and all stored aggregates match exactly. At source_revision, all core_paid and match_paid counts remain unchanged; only core_cost and match_cost increase, by 1.51-2.00%. IRS seed, census, wait configurations, and absolute $0.01 tolerance are unchanged.
earned_compensation_reconciliation.historical_explanation: The explanation document above describes the earlier #889 IRS-seed reconciliation; its pre-raise compensation-basis discussion predates #978/#979.

deferral_rate_timing_reconciliation.basis: Employee deferrals, and the match on them, are weighted by when each deferral rate was in effect during the year.
deferral_rate_timing_reconciliation.verification: With #986 participant behaviors pinned off in the fixture, the isolated characterization test passes against the prior baseline at pre-#1028 revision 306eb045. At #1028, all core_cost, core_paid and match_paid values are unchanged; only match_cost moves, by -0.34% to 0.00%. IRS seed, census, wait configurations and the absolute $0.01 tolerance are unchanged.

age_tenure_progression_reconciliation.basis: Age and tenure now advance once per year instead of twice, so age- and tenure-based eligibility no longer drifts ahead in later years.
age_tenure_progression_reconciliation.verification: Regenerated from isolated runs of all four wait cases at c435ccf; values reproduce CI's failing run exactly. Opening-year values and all core_paid/match_paid counts are unchanged; only zero-wait core_cost and match_cost for 2027-2029 move, by -0.12% to -0.02%. IRS seed, census, wait configurations and the absolute $0.01 tolerance are unchanged.

new_hire_calibration_reconciliation.basis: #1048 applies second-year new-hire turnover to census employees hired in the prior year, indexes new-hire starting pay, spreads hire dates across the year and hires by level. In 2025 the census has 8 experienced terminations instead of 11, so 3 more long-service employees stay and become eligible. #1051 (hire-date and termination fixes) and #1050 (promotion-aware hiring) move later zero-wait costs by under 1%.
new_hire_calibration_reconciliation.verification: Regenerated from isolated runs of all four wait cases at 365f5460. The same harness at the pre-#1048 revision 9fcd74d8 reproduces the prior baseline exactly. The wait-1 opening-year counts (141, 109) match CI's failing runs from a5ef9a9d onward. Opening-year values come entirely from #1048. Zero-wait costs fall 3.3-7.2%, mostly from #1048. IRS seed, census, wait configurations and the absolute $0.01 tolerance are unchanged.
